content: I'll start by reading the test image to analyze its visual features.

The test image shows a sugarcane leaf with:
- Broad longitudinal yellowing/tan-brown discoloration along the margins
- Some residual green near the midrib
- No discrete spots — a diffuse, bleaching/scalding pattern running the leaf length
- The affected margins appear dried and pale tan to brown

This pattern is most suggestive of **Leaf_Scald**. Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The Leaf_Scald reference shows white pencil-line streaks on a mostly green leaf — that's quite different from the test image's broad, extensive tan/yellow-brown discoloration.

Reassessing the test image features:
- **Broad, diffuse yellowing/tan-brown** covering most of the leaf surface (not discrete spots)
- **Green zone retained near one margin/midrib area**
- **Tan to orange-brown at the leaf edges** — suggesting advanced tissue death
- No discrete spots, no striped mosaic pattern

This extensive diffuse yellowing spreading across the leaf lamina with some green retained near the midrib is characteristic of **Yellow_Leaf** disease (Sugarcane yellow leaf virus), which causes progressive yellowing starting from the midrib/underside and spreading across the leaf, ultimately leading to this tan-brown dried appearance at more advanced stages.
